column5: Check rules for NSERC and McMaster logos
column11: Rules checked and written into README §16. McMaster: faculty/staff may use the logo for McMaster initiatives (research groups/centres); a research-group website needs an approved logo lockup requested via Brand Marketing's Logo Request Form (brandmrk@mcmaster.ca); min 100 px, keep clear space, never alter/redraw. NSERC: grantees are required to acknowledge NSERC and may use the NSERC signature (download from nserc-crsng.canada.ca → Acknowledgement and logos); min 100 px, clear space = half the symbol height, NSERC red #DF202D, Canada wordmark must stay.
column12: Action for PJK: submit the McMaster Logo Request Form (or forward the approved files); download the NSERC digital colour signature. The site currently shows text-only placeholder wordmarks. NSERC also encourages a bilingual project description on funded websites — a French summary paragraph is a small follow-up if wanted.

column5: "The blinded evaluation uses 144 cycles at six temperatures" is not quite right; tests go beyond the cycles
column11: Resolved: one shared sentence (EVALUATION_SCOPE in src/lib/test-cases.ts) used everywhere: "144 blinded drive cycles (four cells, six temperatures from −20 °C to 40 °C) plus the robustness tests — wrong initial SOC, current-sensor offsets and charging profiles — 195 evaluation runs in all". Landing hero, stats tile ("144 + 51 blinded drive cycles + robustness runs"), test-run result box and the Methodology page updated.

column5: Plotted results when testing a model are inconsistent with the numbers above (6.1 % max error vs 5.5 % in the plot)
column11: Resolved: traces are down-sampled to ~240 points for display and the sample with the largest error was usually dropped. The evaluator now always keeps the max-|error| sample in every plotted trace (test runs and full evaluations), so the plot's peak equals the reported max error.
column12: Applies to evaluations run after this deploy; older stored traces keep the old down-sampling.

column5: Submitting gives a choice for static evaluation, not sure what this means
column11: Resolved: the "Evaluation level" (dynamic/static) selector is removed from the submit form; every submission is evaluated the same way. The field still exists in the database for the historical rows.
column12: The dynamic/static distinction came from the old site and was never defined for the new evaluator. If a second evaluation mode is ever wanted (e.g. characterisation-only), it can be re-added.

column5: When submitting, should be able to use the same model already uploaded in the testing section
column11: Resolved: after a successful test run there is a "Use this package for the submission" button; it fills the upload box of the submission form with the same .zip and scrolls to it, so only the details need typing.

column5: "Structural checks" run instantly — consider different terminology
column11: Resolved: "package checks (layout, file names, function signature)" everywhere (submit form, confirmation banner, Methodology page, submit page header).

column5: The specific plots generated by the MATLAB script (edge/varying conditions) must be included in the results
column11: Resolved (first version): every result now has a "Key cases" tab with three groups and a one-line "why this case" under each plot — (a) the thirteen drive cycles Create_Figures.m plots — m448N vs m448 LA92 10 °C, m80 US06 25 °C + m80 CC-CV charge 25 °C, m80/m448/m1000 UDDS 10 °C, m1000 HWFET/HWCUST/HWGRADE 25 °C, m80 UDDS −20/0/40 °C; (b) wrong-initial-SOC runs — 3 cycles × 90/60/30 % starts; (c) current-sensor-offset runs — 3 cycles × ±0.3 A. The evaluator stores these traces for every new evaluation. The Time-domain tab keeps the drive cycles for browsing.
column12: Case list taken from Create_Figures.m in the Blind Model Files (Ahnaf version) — all its time-domain panels are covered; the RMSE-vs-offset and RMSE-vs-temperature bar charts exist as the Summary charts. The set is a Python constant (TRACES / CYCLE_NOTES / robustness_traces in evaluator/python/socbench_eval/pipeline.py) and cheap to change. Results evaluated before 8/29 show a note that robustness traces were not recorded. PDF report still shows the 8 drive cycles — adding the robustness plots to the PDF is a follow-up.

column5: Slider bar under plots (time-axis zoom) is sticky and only moves a little
column11: Resolved: replaced the chart library's brush with a custom navigator — the window follows the mouse pixel-for-pixel, either edge can be dragged, dragging inside moves the whole window, dragging outside draws a new one.
column12: The rectangle-zoom tools above the plot (Zoom / Zoom X / Zoom Y / Pan, +/−, Fit, wheel) were also reworked earlier this week to behave like MATLAB figures.
